prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1014; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured vehicle reportedly backed into a parked vehicle while the lot was busy. Claimant reports a wrist fracture from the incident and states she was seated in her vehicle at the time of impact. No attorney listed. Initial contact made by phone; claimant agreed to send photos and medical paperwork.

Entry 2: Received photos of both vehicles from the claimant. Rear bumper damage to the insured vehicle is visible, along with a cracked taillight lens and a dented quarter panel on the claimant's vehicle. Scene photos show parking lot signage and the approximate position of both cars. Insured's statement obtained; he says he did not see the claimant's vehicle before reversing. Requested the store's security footage through the property manager.

Entry 3: Claimant provided an urgent care discharge summary confirming a wrist fracture and a splint. She states she is right-hand dominant and has been unable to drive or work since the incident. Reviewed policy limits and coverage for bodily injury and property damage; no coverage issues identified at this stage. Advised claimant that she may wish to seek her own medical follow-up and keep all receipts. Claimant asked how the process works and whether she needs to do anything else; explained the next steps in general terms.

Entry 4: Store security footage received and reviewed. Footage shows the insured vehicle reversing from a parking space and making contact with the claimant's vehicle at low speed. Claimant's vehicle was stopped with its engine running. Witness statement from a nearby shopper was obtained by phone and corroborates the account. Liability appears to rest primarily with the insured. Property damage estimate requested from the preferred repair facility.

Entry 5: Repair estimate for the claimant's vehicle received. Claimant has requested a rental vehicle while repairs are completed and asked for an update on the bodily injury portion. Requested updated medical records and an itemized list of treatment and expenses from the claimant. Reserves reviewed and adjusted pending receipt of records. Diary set for follow-up in two weeks or sooner if new documentation arrives.
